c.pop: ~25 (commune; a working abbey and hotel village)
c.tagline: A tidal island abbey rising from the sand, France's most-visited landmark outside Paris

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small shops on the mount
rides: Free shuttle from the mainland parking area
local taxi companies from nearby towns

taxi.fare: Flat rate typically negotiated for transfers from nearby towns
taxi.fareNote: Most visitors arrive via the free shuttle from the mainland car park rather than a taxi directly to the mount

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

religion: Roman Catholic (the abbey remains an active monastic community)
walk: The mount itself is compact but steep, with a single main pedestrian street and ramparts walk; the surrounding bay must only be crossed with a guide due to dangerous tides and quicksand

safety.safety: Very safe, though the bay's tides are genuinely dangerous — never walk into the bay without a licensed guide
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded midday periods is the main concern; the real hazard is the tide, not crime

hood_landmark.The Abbey: The Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey church and cloister
hood_landmark.Grande Rue: The Grande Rue's medieval shops and La Mere Poulard restaurant
hood_landmark.Ramparts: The fortified ramparts walk encircling the village
hood_landmark.Mainland Visitor Village: The mainland shuttle terminal and visitor center
hood_landmark.Bay Crossing Area: The tidal bay's guided low-tide walking routes

avoid.reason: Never walk the bay sands without a licensed guide — fast tides and quicksand are genuinely dangerous; expect a midday tour-bus crush on the Grande Rue.

hood_desc: The Gothic-Romanesque abbey crowning the mount, the reason the site exists and the highlight of any visit.
The single steep pedestrian street winding up from the gate, lined with souvenir shops, crêperies, and the famous Mère Poulard omelette restaurant.
The fortified walls circling the base of the mount, offering some of the best photo views back toward the abbey.
The mainland hub a couple km away with parking, hotels, and the free shuttle bus or footbridge walk to the mount.
The vast tidal bay surrounding the mount, walkable only with a licensed guide due to fast-moving tides and quicksand.
lodging: Mainland hotels near the shuttle terminal

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.sys: Free shuttle bus (navette) between the mainland car park and the mount
transit.note: Private cars are not permitted onto the mount itself; visitors park on the mainland and take the shuttle or walk the footbridge

transport.air: Rennes Airport (RNS) or Caen-Carpiquet, both roughly 1-1.5 hr away
transport.train: Nearest TGV stations are Rennes or Pontorson-Mont-Saint-Michel, connected by shuttle bus
transport.bus: Direct shuttle buses run seasonally from Rennes, Saint-Malo, and Pontorson
transport.car: A large mainland car park serves the site; the mount itself is car-free

airport.name: Rennes Airport (main regional gateway)
airport.transport: Shuttle bus, train plus bus, or rental car

net.m: Good 4G coverage on the mount and mainland
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An Orange, SFR, or Bouygues tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for bay-crossing guides
tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up is a nice gesture, not expected
